title: Filmic Faded
description: A filmic faded grade in filmic color grade work imitates a print: blacks are lifted off true zero, highlights roll off instead of clipping like video, and contrast sits like photochemical display. It is not HDR punch, and it is not automatically period costume.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The image looks like it could have gone through a projector. Shadows have air.
Bright windows go creamy instead of digital-clipped. Romance and memory often live here because the display already forgives, but the hues can still be present and modern.

It is the wrong tool when you need packed, merciless blacks (Bleach Bypass or a hard digital contrast). It is the wrong tool if the fade is meant as expired dyes and period chemistry as a whole costume: that is Vintage.
Vintage Cine Glass is the taking lens; you can shoot modern glass and still fade the print. Film Grain is texture you may add, not the fade itself.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Lift the toe (blacks sit at a low grey, not 0). Roll the shoulder so highlights compress instead of hard-clipping.
Keep saturation moderate unless the story is candy. A print-emulation LUT is a starting point; still check skin and that blacks are lifted, not milky-brown by accident.
Prompt: Filmic faded grade on [Subject], lifted blacks, rolled-off highlights, print-emulation, slightly expired romance.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the display should feel like a print rather than HDR: a summer memory, a period-adjacent present. Do not use it on a look that needs crushed blacks, and do not treat fade as a substitute for vintage glass.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Bleach Bypass (packed, harsh) or a milky brown wash. The tell is crushed blacks, or a foggy image with no rolled shoulder.
Fix: lifted toe, compressed highlights, hues still present, contrast like a print.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is filmic faded in film?
It is a print-emulation grade: lifted blacks, rolled-off highlights, contrast that sits like photochemical display rather than HDR video. Hues may still be present.
Filmic Faded vs Vintage Cine Glass

Vintage cine is the taking lens: coatings, swirl, optical bloom. Filmic faded is the curve of the grade: toe and shoulder of a print. You can fade a modern prime, and you can shoot old glass without lifting the blacks.
When should I use filmic faded?
Use it when the image should feel like a print, not like HDR. Skip it when blacks must pack down, or when you only needed grain or old glass.
How do I prompt filmic faded for AI image or video?
Write: Filmic faded grade on [Subject], lifted blacks, rolled-off highlights, print-emulation, slightly expired romance. Forbid crushed bleach-bypass blacks and HDR clip.
